propositions: The 798-line compact.py bundles three responsibilities (transaction logic, snapshot reconstruction, CLI) with high cyclomatic complexity (functions up to CCN 24), triggering an audit flag and blocking unrelated bug fixes.

Splitting compact.py into two focused modules (compact_txn.py for transactions and shared primitives; compact_rebuild.py for rebuild logic) requires all snapshot helpers in compact_txn to avoid circular imports between the two new modules.

The _REBUILD_COUNT global and its accessor get_rebuild_count must co-locate in compact_rebuild.py with rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log (which references the global directly), while being re-exported from compact.py for backward compatibility.

Module monkeypatch seams in test_compact_negative.py that patch _git and lock on the _compact module object must be repointed to compact_txn._git and _lock respectively, since _compact_locked now reads compact_txn's module globals.

The refactored compact.py retains CLI entry points and re-exports all public symbols for consumers (fsck_repair.py, fsck_restore.py, tests), keeping _cli/__init__.py unchanged and maintaining import paths.
